corrections.prior: Paired gonads that contain seminiferous tubules for sperm development and interstitial cells that produce testosterone.
corrections.corrected: Paired reproductive organs that support sperm development and release hormones, including testosterone.

corrections.prior: A coiled testicular tubule where sperm cells develop with Sertoli-cell support.
corrections.corrected: Coiled tubes inside the testes where sperm cells develop among supporting cells.

corrections.prior: A supporting cell within a seminiferous tubule that helps regulate and nourish developing sperm cells.
corrections.corrected: Supporting cells within the sperm-producing tubes of a testis; they nourish developing sperm and regulate their local conditions.

corrections.prior: A testicular cell between seminiferous tubules that produces testosterone in response to LH.
corrections.corrected: Cells between the sperm-producing tubes of a testis that release the hormone testosterone into blood; also called Leydig cells.

corrections.prior: A muscular duct, also called the vas deferens, that transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct.
corrections.corrected: A muscular duct that transports sperm from the epididymis toward the ejaculatory duct; also called the ductus deferens.

corrections.prior: A male accessory gland that contributes a substantial portion of seminal fluid.
corrections.corrected: Paired glands that add a substantial part of the fluid in semen; they do not produce sperm.

corrections.prior: An accessory gland, also called a Cowper’s gland, that releases fluid into the male reproductive tract.
corrections.corrected: Small glands below the prostate that release fluid into the urethra; also called bulbourethral glands.

corrections.prior: A steroid androgen produced mainly by testicular interstitial cells and involved in reproductive function and development.
corrections.corrected: A chemical messenger made mainly by cells between the sperm-producing tubes of the testes; it contributes to reproductive development, function and feedback.

corrections.prior: A diploid germ-line stem or precursor cell that divides mitotically and can enter spermatogenesis.
corrections.corrected: A precursor cell in the sperm-producing lineage with two chromosome sets; its divisions can maintain precursor cells and produce cells that develop toward sperm.

corrections.prior: A differentiated sperm cell specialized for carrying a haploid genome and interacting with an oocyte.
corrections.corrected: A specialized sperm cell carrying one chromosome set and able, under suitable conditions, to interact with a developing egg cell.

corrections.prior: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone; a hypothalamic signal that stimulates anterior-pituitary release of FSH and LH.
corrections.corrected: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone: a chemical signal from the brain region called the hypothalamus that stimulates release of FSH and LH from the front part of the pituitary gland.

corrections.prior: Follicle-stimulating hormone; an anterior-pituitary gonadotropin that supports ovarian follicle development and acts through Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis.
corrections.corrected: Follicle-stimulating hormone: a signal from the anterior pituitary that supports growth of the cells around a developing egg and acts through Sertoli cells to support sperm development.

corrections.prior: Luteinizing hormone; an anterior-pituitary gonadotropin involved in ovulation and corpus-luteum formation and in testicular testosterone production.
corrections.corrected: Luteinizing hormone: a signal from the anterior pituitary that stimulates testosterone release in testes and helps trigger egg release and formation of temporary hormone-producing tissue in ovaries.

corrections.prior: A brain region that integrates information and releases signals such as GnRH to help regulate pituitary activity.
corrections.corrected: A brain region that integrates information and releases signals to help regulate the pituitary gland.

corrections.prior: The glandular front part of the pituitary; it releases hormones including FSH, LH and prolactin.
corrections.corrected: The hormone-producing front part of the pituitary gland below the brain.

corrections.prior: A gonad that contains developing oocytes and produces reproductive hormones.
corrections.corrected: A reproductive organ that contains developing egg cells and releases reproductive hormones.

corrections.prior: Temporary endocrine tissue formed from an ovulated follicle that produces progesterone and estrogen.
corrections.corrected: Temporary hormone-producing tissue formed from a follicle after ovulation; it releases progesterone and estrogen.

corrections.prior: The biological capacity or probability of reproduction, influenced by many interacting factors and not established by one classroom measure.
corrections.corrected: The chance of a specified reproductive outcome under stated conditions; it depends on many factors and is not established by one classroom measurement.

corrections.prior: The extracellular glycoprotein layer surrounding the oocyte and early conceptus before hatching.
corrections.corrected: The protective protein-and-sugar layer around a developing egg cell and the early developing cell group before it hatches from this layer.

corrections.prior: A compact early ball of blastomeres formed during cleavage before the blastocyst stage.
corrections.corrected: A compact ball of cells formed by early divisions after fertilization, before a fluid-filled blastocyst develops.

corrections.prior: The outer epithelial layer of skin; it is distinct from deeper connective tissue.
corrections.corrected: The outer surface layer of skin, distinct from the deeper supporting tissue.

corrections.prior: The epithelial tissue facing the internal space of the digestive tract.
corrections.corrected: The layer of cells facing the internal space of the digestive tract.

corrections.prior: The epithelial tissue facing the air passages of the respiratory system.
corrections.corrected: The layer of cells facing the air passages of the respiratory system.

corrections.prior: Distortion that occurs when another factor is related to both the proposed cause and the measured outcome.
corrections.corrected: Another factor related to both the proposed cause and the measured outcome, which can distort the apparent relationship between them.

corrections.prior: A posterior-pituitary-released hormone involved in uterine contraction and milk ejection.
corrections.corrected: A hormone made in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior pituitary; it contributes to uterine contraction and milk ejection.

corrections.prior: Oxytocin-supported contraction of myoepithelial cells that moves milk through mammary ducts.
corrections.corrected: Movement of milk into mammary ducts when surrounding contractile cells respond to oxytocin; it differs from making milk.
